purpose: Fresh transfer test for a fusion policy frozen using DEV only.

tasks.prompt: Return only the integer result: 58 + 67.
Return only the integer result: 17 * 8.
Return only the integer result: 225 / 15.
Return only the integer result: 3^5.

Return only A, B, C, or D. A model improves on training data but worsens on both transfer and red-team sets. Which claim is supported? A: General improvement. B: Training fit improved but generalization is not supported. C: G7 is proven. D: The red-team set should be deleted.

Return only A, B, C, or D. Three reports cite the same underlying dataset and reach the same conclusion. How many independent data lineages are demonstrated? A: Three. B: One unless other independence is shown. C: Zero automatically. D: Six.

Return only A, B, C, or D. A physical simulation matches its own synthetic generator exactly. What is established? A: Real-world validation. B: Internal consistency in that simulator, not physical calibration. C: Universal law. D: Independent experiment.

Return only A, B, C, or D. A benchmark was used to choose among ten prompt variants. Can it still be called untouched cold evidence for the chosen prompt? A: Yes. B: No, selection used it. C: Only if the score is high. D: Only with more agents.
Return only one word: CALCULATOR, WEB, PYTHON, GITHUB, or MEMORY. You need the current release notes for a software library.
Return only one word: CALCULATOR, WEB, PYTHON, GITHUB, or MEMORY. You need to inspect whether a particular commit changed a workflow file.
Return only one word: CALCULATOR, WEB, PYTHON, GITHUB, or MEMORY. You need to sort and aggregate one million local rows.
Return only one word: CALCULATOR, WEB, PYTHON, GITHUB, or MEMORY. You need a previously stored project checkpoint from prior conversations.

Return only A, B, C, or D. Core A scores 18/24, Core B scores 14/24, fusion scores 18/24 but doubles latency with no risk reduction. What does ablation support? A: Keep fusion by default. B: Prefer A for that scope. C: Count two proofs. D: Promote fusion globally.

Return only A, B, C, or D. A critic catches two errors but also changes three correct answers into wrong ones. What is the first conclusion? A: Critic gate needs repair. B: Promote immediately. C: Ignore harmful replacements. D: Call the critic independent proof.

Return only A, B, C, or D. A candidate passes validation but has zero transfer gain where the gate requires strictly positive transfer. What is the gate status? A: PASS. B: FAIL or HOLD. C: G7. D: Runtime default.

Return only A, B, C, or D. A training run changes no weights. Which statement is correct? A: Neural learning is verified. B: Neural training success is not established. C: It is automatically G6. D: It proves transfer.
Return only the integer result. A test has 64 cases and 75 percent pass. How many pass?
Return only the integer result. A fusion resolves 21 of 28 cases. What is coverage percent rounded to the nearest integer?
Return only the integer result. A baseline has 13 errors and a repaired system has 8. How many errors were removed?

Return only A, B, C, or D. Two model cores disagree and neither critique resolves the conflict. What should a contradiction-preserving system do? A: Pretend consensus. B: Preserve unresolved status or abstain. C: Pick the longer answer. D: Count both as true.

Return only A, B, C, or D. A new fusion policy was selected using DEV. What must happen before a cold test? A: Keep changing the policy during the test. B: Freeze the policy. C: Add the cold answers to memory. D: Train on the cold set.

Return only A, B, C, or D. A cold test is passed once, then its answers are used to revise the policy and it is run again. How should the second run be treated? A: Fresh independent cold evidence. B: Post-selection evidence, not untouched cold. C: A proof. D: A new model lineage.

Return only A, B, C, or D. A second core improves accuracy by one point but increases critical-error rate. Which rule dominates? A: Accuracy alone. B: No critical-regression gate. C: Majority vote. D: Model size.

Return only A, B, C, or D. Four successful workflows share the same model, code, and dataset. How many independent evidence lines are proven by workflow count alone? A: Four. B: One. C: Zero independent lines are proven by count alone. D: Eight.
